title: Open the global search palette with the keyboard shortcut (⌘K / Ctrl+K)
preconds: 1. Sign in to ShopView and go to any page, for example the Work Orders list. The persistent search field in the app header shows the shortcut hint (for example 'Search ⌘K').
steps:
1. Without clicking anything, press ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows), as shown in the header search field.
2. Watch the screen.
expected:
1. A centered search box (a modal overlay, 640px wide) opens on top of the page, positioned 96px from the top — it is NOT anchored to the header field.

2. The page behind the box is dimmed.

3. The search input is focused so you can type right away, and shows the placeholder 'Search work orders, customers, parts and more' (no 'ask a question' / AI wording — AI is out of scope in v1).

4. The footer keyboard legend is visible: ↓↑ Navigate · ⏎ Select · Esc Close.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 5.1 (trigger and surface), read on 16 September 2026.

Note: earlier this case gave only 'a plain search placeholder'. Spec v1.3 (2026-09-01, §5.1) fixes the exact placeholder and that the modal is centered (not anchored to the header); this case follows the current spec.

Last checked against build v26.36.7-21b4db9 on 9/16/2026.

1. Sign in and open global search: click the Search box in the app header, or press Ctrl+K. It opens a centred modal — a search box, a scope-tab strip (All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices) each with its own count, and results grouped by type with a count on each heading; press Esc to close. Seed check: if a search for ZZAUTOTEST returns nothing the build was redeployed, so ask for a reseed and do not hand-create records.
1. Search for ZZAUTOTEST, which returns several different kinds of record at once - a customer, an asset, a vendor, a part and work orders.
2. Access to all of those areas.
steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type: ZZAUTOTEST
3. Look at the left-hand side of every result row.
4. Check that a customer row, an asset row, a vendor row, a part row and a work order row each carry an icon, and that rows of the SAME kind carry the SAME icon.
expected:
Every result row shows a small icon on its left, and the icon differs by record type so you can tell at a glance what each row is.
In V1 each type had its own icon: a building for a customer, a contact card for a contact match, a truck for an asset, a shopfront for a vendor, and a tools icon for work orders, part sales and parts.
The exact pictures may differ in V2 - what must not happen is rows losing their icon, or every type showing the same one, because then you can no longer tell the kinds apart while scanning.

title: Typing a name does not bring back other differently spelled names
preconds:
1. Sign in and open global search: click the Search box in the app header, or press Ctrl+K. It opens a centred modal — a search box, a scope-tab strip (All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices) each with its own count, and results grouped by type with a count on each heading; press Esc to close. Seed check: if a search for ZZAUTOTEST returns nothing the build was redeployed, so ask for a reseed and do not hand-create records.
1. Two customers exist, both created by the seeding script (build/global-search/seeding/seed.py - run it after every redeploy or this test is meaningless): ZZAUTOTEST Marlene Freight Lines and ZZAUTOTEST Darlene Cartage.
2. These two names differ by exactly ONE letter - M against D. That is the whole point of the pair: one of them contains the word you are going to type and the other does not.
3. Wait about 30 seconds after seeding before searching, so both records are in the search index.
steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type: Marlene
3. Wait for the results to finish loading, then read EVERY row in EVERY group - scroll the whole list.
4. Write down each row that does NOT contain the word you typed, and which group it was in.
5. Click the Customers tab and check that list too.
expected:
Every record that comes back contains the word you typed. ZZAUTOTEST Marlene Freight Lines is there. ZZAUTOTEST Darlene Cartage is NOT - you did not type Darlene.
In V1 search compared the letters you typed against the letters in the record. A record came back only if it actually contained what you typed, so a name spelled differently was never returned. Typing a person's name gave you that person.
THIS IS EXPECTED TO DIFFER ON THE CURRENT BUILD. V2 also returns records whose wording is merely CLOSE to what you typed - close enough that two letters may differ. Measured live on the V2 QA branch on 14 September 2026, typing Marlene returned 18 rows and only TWO of them genuinely contained the word. The other sixteen were Darlene (contact names), Charlene (street addresses), Martens (company names), Marine (battery terminal parts) and Alene (from the vendor Coeur d'Alene) - five words nobody typed. ZZAUTOTEST Darlene Cartage will be one of them, and its appearing is exactly the symptom this case exists to record.
THE TICKET IS ALREADY RAISED - SV-10025 - so do NOT raise another one. It was filed by the QA lead on 14 September 2026 and the exact query above is the example in it: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10025
WHAT TO DO, depending on what you see:
(1) You see exactly what is described above - the extra words are there - then mark this test FAILED, write down the rows that did not contain what you typed, and raise NOTHING new. That is the known problem.
(2) It fails DIFFERENTLY - the record you typed is missing altogether, or a completely different kind of unrelated record comes back - then that is a NEW problem. Report it separately with the exact query and what came back.
(3) It PASSES - only records containing what you typed come back - then the fix has shipped. Tell the QA lead so SV-10025 can be closed and this case turned into an ordinary passing case.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test FAILED and write down the exact words you typed and what came back. It worked in the previous version, so it has to work here - failing is a fault and a ticket is raised against it. Do not pass the test just because the newer specification allows the new behaviour.

---

This is the expected behaviour as per the V1 product itself: the ShopView product repository at commit 55767168, useGlobalSearch.ts:76-92, where the first pass asks whether the record's name STARTS WITH the typed text and the second asks whether the record's combined text CONTAINS it. Both are literal letter-for-letter comparisons - there is no allowance in V1 for a near spelling.
For this V1 regression suite the shipped V1 product IS the specification (Standing Rule 109). Epic SV-9160 is the project this work belongs to, not the source of this expectation, and anything quoted below from the V2 requirements is context only - never the authority for this case. section: Global Search V2 - V1 Regression Suite
title: Finding an asset by its make on its own
preconds:
1. Sign in and open global search: click the Search box in the app header, or press Ctrl+K. It opens a centred modal — a search box, a scope-tab strip (All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices) each with its own count, and results grouped by type with a count on each heading; press Esc to close. Seed check: if a search for ZZAUTOTEST returns nothing the build was redeployed, so ask for a reseed and do not hand-create records.
1. The asset '2019 Freightliner Cascadia', unit number 'ZZT-4471', owned by 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', exists.
2. Freightliner is the MAKE. Cascadia is the model. This case tests the make.
3. Customers access: View (assets are shown under Customers access).
steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the make on its own: Freightliner
3. Read the Assets group. Look at the make of every vehicle listed.
Type the make and nothing else. Do not add the year or the model - typing the year together with the make is a different test with a different result, and it has its own case.
The list shows a limited number of vehicles per group, and a busy shop has far more vehicles of one make or one year than the list can show. So your seeded vehicle may or may not be among them, and its absence is not a failure - what matters is whether the search used the field at all.
expected:
Every vehicle listed in the Assets group is a Freightliner, and the group is not empty. That is what proves the search looked at the vehicle's make.
In V1 the make was part of what a vehicle could be found by, in its own right - alongside the year, the model, the unit number, the VIN number and the licence plate.

WHAT COUNTS AS A FAILURE, and what does not.
A failure: the Assets group is empty, or vehicles of a DIFFERENT make appear in it.
Not a failure: your own seeded vehicle '2019 Freightliner Cascadia' is not in the list. There are more Freightliners in this data than the list can show, so it may sit below the last row. V1 showed even fewer per group than V2 does, so this was never a case of 'my vehicle must appear' - it is a case of 'the make is searched'. If you want to see that exact vehicle, search its model instead - that is C55664.
Also not a failure: a vehicle whose displayed make looks unrelated but whose VIN number or unit number contains the letters you typed. Open the record and check before calling it wrong - those fields are searched too.

---
SOURCE - THIS CASE IS TESTED AGAINST V1, NOT AGAINST THE V2 SPECIFICATION.
This is the expected behaviour as per the V1 product itself: the ShopView product repository at commit 55767168, FetchDataQueryHandler.php:288 - the vehicle make is folded into the asset search text (V1 invariant INV-04). V1 also showed at most three rows per group (useGlobalSearch.ts, MAX_PER_TYPE = 3), which is why the V1 capability is that the make is SEARCHED, not that any particular vehicle appears.
For this V1 regression suite the shipped V1 product IS the specification (Standing Rule 109). Epic SV-9160 is the project this work belongs to, not the source of this expectation, and anything quoted below from the V2 requirements is context only - never the authority for this case. Version 1.5 of the specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 lists the asset make among the things indexed.
Where V2 differs from V1 the difference is raised as a finding and a task ticket for the Product Owner, never adopted as the expectation (Standing Rules 96 and 58).

1. You are signed in as a user with access to BOTH locations - Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
2. You are currently on Heavy Duty.

HOW TO GET A WORK ORDER NUMBER TO TYPE — do this first, it takes five seconds. Open global search and type ZZAUTOTEST. The Work orders group lists our 20 test jobs. Write down the number of any one of them — it looks like S-17611. Use THAT number wherever these steps say "the work order number". Why you are asked to look it up instead of being given one: the job numbers change every time a new build is put on this branch, so any number printed here would be wrong within days. The number on screen is always right.
steps:
1. On Heavy Duty, open global search and type: Bridgeport
2. Confirm the four work orders appear.
3. WITHOUT closing search, switch the location to Lethbridge.
4. Search Bridgeport again and watch the results CLOSELY as they load - including the moment before the new results settle.
5. Repeat the switch a few times, watching each time.
expected:
After the switch, the Heavy Duty work orders are gone and they are never shown even for a moment while the new results are loading.
The customer itself still appears at both locations - customers belong to the whole company - but its WORK ORDERS belong to Heavy Duty and must not follow you to Lethbridge, not even briefly.
In V1 the old location's rows were cleared the instant you switched, before the new ones were fetched, precisely so nothing from the other location could flash on screen. A brief flash is still a user seeing records from a location they have switched away from.
